title: Costa Mesa Police drone flights, DFR pilot and Skydio-Axon purchase

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Costa Mesa Police drone flights, DFR pilot and Skydio-Axon purchase
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records concerning the Costa Mesa Police Department’s unmanned aerial systems (UAS) and Drone as First Responder (DFR) program, including:

1. Flight and deployment logs for April 18, 2025, through October 6, 2026, including the reported 459 deployments in fiscal year 2025–26 and DFR operations at South Coast Plaza. Please include available dates and times, general locations, call-for-service or incident identifiers, flight duration, outcomes, and any records showing who accessed or viewed recorded footage.

2. Records evaluating the three-week DFR pilot conducted with Skydio Inc. in May and June 2025, including the evaluation, operational data, pilot plans, reports, and communications about results or recommendations.

3. Records concerning the City Council’s October 6, 2026, approval of a two-year purchase from Axon Enterprise Inc. (Skydio Inc.) under Omnia Contract No. 3544-21-4615, including the purchase agreement and amendments, quote 834688-004, statement of work, purchase orders, invoices, grant-funding records, and implementation plans for the Skydio X-10 drone and three docking stations.

4. Current CMPD Policy 606 and records governing DFR deployment, footage retention, access, sharing, public disclosure, and audit logs for footage stored in Axon Evidence.

Please search records held by Capt. Carlos Diaz, Lt. Nick Wilson, the Police Department personnel responsible for UAS operations and procurement, and the City Clerk/City Manager’s offices, including communications with Axon Enterprise Inc. or Skydio Inc. from May 1, 2025, through October 6, 2026, concerning the pilot, DFR operations, data or footage, and the approved purchase.

Source: https://www.latimes.com/socal/daily-pilot/news/story/2026-10-07/as-costa-mesa-mulls-surveillance-privacy-police-expand-drone-force

Please waive any fees, as these records will be used in the course of reporting for 404media.co.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jason Koebler

communications.subject: Nebraska Public Records Act Request: Deaths-in-custody
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Nebraska Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

The database or records of all law enforcement agencies deaths-in-custody up to the date this request is ultimately fulfilled, including all deaths-in-custody reported pursuant to federal legislation (34 U.S.C. § 60105), as well as all data dictionaries, database scheme documentation or other documentation on the collection and organization of the data. 

I request these records in their native digital formats and not in formats that degrade the accessibility of the records, such as tabular data converted to PDF or Word files. If converting the native digital format to another high-fidelity format, such as CSV or Excel, please take care not to introduce formatting inconsistencies or errors, which can occur in the conversion process (for example, encoding errors or the inclusion of internal unescaped quotation marks in CSV files). Should the records above represent certain values as numeric codes or abbreviations that are not self-explanatory, we additionally request all records necessary to interpret those codes and abbreviations.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 4 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Dillon Bergin

title: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Franklin Police Department)

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Franklin Police Department)
communications.communication:
Dear Record Access Officer:

This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1.    All municipal or police department policies, ordinances, or resolutions currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and federal agents/agencies within the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including but not limited to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:

             A. Fingerprint and other data sharing;
             B. Compliance with federal immigration enforcement efforts, including guidance or policies concerning when communication with ICE officers is allowed. This includes how and under what circumstances to respond to ICE detainer requests or when and how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances;
             C. Any other records that indicate changes in policy or practice as a result of the passage of the Massachusetts PROTECT Act in August 2026.

 2.  All departmental and municipal policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of local resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies, requests or responses to requests for the use of municipal parking lots, police station interior or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.

3.    Any records of email, text, or phone conversations between department employees and federal DHS employees working at ICE made from September 4, 2026 until October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026), including but not limited to email sent to any “@ice.dhs.gov” email address. This request includes any call logs or transcripts of calls.

For each request, I am not seeking identifying information of community members, and I will accept anonymized or redacted data as necessary to protect the identity of the public. Redaction of names of municipal, state, or federal government employees is not necessary.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. The Public Records Law requires a written response within 10 business days. If you cannot comply with my request, you are statutorily required to provide an explanation in writing.

Sincerely,

Joshua Dankoff
Director of Strategic Initaitives
Citizens for Juvenile Justice
joshuadankoff@cfjj.org
(submitted via muckrock)

communications.subject: Government Records Access and Management Act Request: UtahMedical Copay Fee Information
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Government Records Access and Management Act, I hereby request the following records:

The following materials regarding the imposition, assessment, collection and balances of inmate fees and debt:

a) All current policies and procedures regarding medical copays or fees for which inmates are or may become liable. Please include all policies and procedures related to how fees are set, accrued, imposed, collected, and enforced (such as those related to per diem fees, ability to pay determinations, penalties for late or non-payment, authorization for civil or criminal action for payment enforcement, etc).

b) All reports, databases, spreadsheets, or equivalent materials regarding total fees collected from inmates for medical copays or fees from 2020-2024. Please include the number of individuals charged for medical costs or fees and the total amount of medical fees imposed this past calendar year. 

If this request is overly burdensome or requires a substantial amount of labor, please provide the materials for the past calendar year.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Watertown Police Department)
communications.communication:
Dear Record Access Officer:

This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1.    All municipal or police department policies, ordinances, or resolutions currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and federal agents/agencies within the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including but not limited to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:

             A. Fingerprint and other data sharing;
             B. Compliance with federal immigration enforcement efforts, including guidance or policies concerning when communication with ICE officers is allowed. This includes how and under what circumstances to respond to ICE detainer requests or when and how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances;
             C. Any other records that indicate changes in policy or practice as a result of the passage of the Massachusetts PROTECT Act in August 2026.

 2.  All departmental and municipal policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of local resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies, requests or responses to requests for the use of municipal parking lots, police station interior or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.

3.    Any records of email, text, or phone conversations between department employees and federal DHS employees working at ICE made from September 4, 2026 until October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026), including but not limited to email sent to any “@ice.dhs.gov” email address. This request includes any call logs or transcripts of calls.

For each request, I am not seeking identifying information of community members, and I will accept anonymized or redacted data as necessary to protect the identity of the public. Redaction of names of municipal, state, or federal government employees is not necessary.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. The Public Records Law requires a written response within 10 business days. If you cannot comply with my request, you are statutorily required to provide an explanation in writing.

Sincerely,

Joshua Dankoff
Director of Strategic Initaitives
Citizens for Juvenile Justice
joshuadankoff@cfjj.org
(submitted via muckrock)

communications.subject: Georgia Open Records Act Request: Flock Safety Event Log, May 15, 2026 to Present
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Georgia Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

I am requesting the Flock Safety Event Log for the Savannah Police Department’s Flock account, covering every organization or network in the account, from May 15, 2026, through the date of this request. This is the export of user and administrative actions with the columns Timestamp, User, Event Type, Entity Type, Entity Details, and Event Id. It is not the license plate search audit.

In priority order:

Every event other than live stream views, for example, network share changes (create, update, or delete), custom hotlist entries, recorded stream views, and stream downloads.
The live stream view events.
Any documentation from Flock or kept by the Department that explains the Event Log’s fields, event types, and entity types.

If item 2 is large or costly, please send items 1 and 3 first and give me the estimate for item 2. I am glad to narrow its date range or scope.

Please provide the log as a CSV or the platform’s native export so I can search it. If the platform limits the export size or period, please provide as many exports as needed to cover the whole period with no gaps, and tell me the first and last event date in each file. This includes records Flock Safety maintains for the Department. See O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(a)(2)(B).

If any part cannot be released, please tell me which part and the specific legal authority by Code section, subsection, and paragraph, as § 50-18-71(d) provides, and release the rest. I do not authorize any work that would exceed $25 until I have approved the estimate.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Ethan Watters

communications.subject: RE: Colorado Open Records Act Request: Douglas County Axon Logs (Douglas County Sheriff)
communications.communication:
Lisa,

The listed reasons for denial of records do not apply in this instance. Please proceed with the records request.

- CRS 42-4-110.5 refers only to automatic vehicle detection systems used to detect traffic violations, which does not apply to ALPR systems, nor their data.

- CRS42-4-110.5(7)(b) specifically refers to images and video, which I did not request. This is ultimately not relevant, as all of CRS 42-4-110.5 does not apply in this situation.

- CRS 42-4-110.5(7)(c) refers to photos, videos or personally identifiable information, which I did not request. Furthermore, per the Douglas County Sheriff Office's website: "ALPR specifically cannot track individuals or capture personal identifiers." And "This method deliberately avoids capturing unnecessary personal details and people."
(https://dcsheriff.net/sheriffs-office/government-transparency/use-of-technology-and-data/)
Again, this point is ultimately not relevant, as all of CRS 42-4-110.5 does not apply in this situation.

- CRS 24-72-305(5) allows for denial of the disclosure of records if such disclosure would be contrary to the public interest. I believe the release of these records is in the public interest. 

Per Douglas County Sheriff Office's website: "all use is subject to audit and oversight."
This should cover the 4 requested records: 
- Internal ALPR Activity Report
- Network ALPR activity Report
- ALPR sharing report
- ALPR Hotlist Management Audit Report

If there are individual redactions that need to be made for the public interest, then please do so. Otherwise, please proceed with the records request. 

Thank you,
William Beckett

1. copy of Silver Star Medal award citation

Korean War

MUCKROCK NEWS Dept MR ##
263 HUNTINGTON AVE
BOSTON, MA 02115
Graduated 1946 from the U.S. Military Academy at West Point, New York. Rheault was awarded the Silver Star for his actions in combat in the Korean War, attaining the rank of captain. After Korea, Rheault taught French at the U.S. Military Academy for several years in the mid-1950s, attaining the rank of major. Rheault attended the Special Forces Qualification course, the Q-Course, in 1961, and his initial Special Forces assignment was with the 10th Special Forces Group in Germany. He would later command the 1st Special Forces Group on Okinawa before being assigned to Vietnam to take command of the 5th Special Forces Group

Please conduct a search of the Central Records System, including but not limited to the Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) Indices, the Microphone Surveillance (MISUR) Indices, the Physical Surveillance (FISUR) Indices, and the Technical Surveillance (TESUR) Indices, for both main-file records and cross-reference records for all relevant names, individuals, agencies and companies. If any potentially responsive records have been destroyed and/or transferred to NARA, then I request copies of the destruction or transfer slips as well as any other documentation relating to, mentioning or describing said transfer or destruction, to include but not be limited to confirmation that the Bureau has no other copies of said records. If previously released records are available, then I request a rolling release consisting of those records while additional records are located and processed for release.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Alexa Gagosz

communications.communication:
Good Morning Alexa Gagosz,

We're contacting you in reference to the FOIPA request number included in the subject line of this email.  The FBI located approximately 1,213 pages potentially responsive to your request.

Requests are processed in the order in which they are received through our multi-track processing system:

Simple track requests (0-50 pages) current average time is approximately 8 months to complete;

Small track requests (51-250 pages) current average time is approximately 36 months to complete;

Medium track requests (251-500 pages) current average time is approximately 44 months to complete;

Large track requests (501-4,999 pages) current average time is approximately 67 months to complete; and

Extra-large track requests (5,000+ pages) current average time is approximately 79 months to complete.

The current average time to complete your large track request is at least 67 months.  Reducing the scope of your request may accelerate the processing, allow for a timelier receipt of the information you seek, and reduce the duplication costs, if applicable.  Would you be willing to consider reducing the scope of your request to place it in a smaller, potentially faster processing track?



Please let us know if this is something you would be interested in further discussing.



Sincerely,

Negotiation Team
Federal Bureau of Investigation

communications.subject: Oregon Public Records Law Request: Talent Police Department Flock Camera policy, invoice, map, and contracts
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Oregon Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

I am requesting a copy of the following records, that have already been requested to Talent Police Department. By requesting previously produced records, I am hopeful that this request will require minimal labor to locate, review and produce the records. Please let me know if you need any additional information or clarification regarding the records I am seeking.

The records I am seeking are:

(1) all policies Talent Police Department has that oversee and/or regulate the operation and use of Automated License Plate Readers, including the operation and use of Flock, Vigilant, Axon, or any similar ALPR programs and softwares
(2) a copy of any and all invoices Talent Police Department has between any and all Automated License Plate Readers softwares and programs, including Flock, Vigilant, Axon, or any similar ALPR programs and softwares
(3) a map of all ALPR cameras that Talent Police Department owns, operates or has access to
(4) a copy of any and all license and user agreements, contracts, memorandums of understanding or other similar type documents that describe and/or regulate the use, retention, collection, and sharing of ALPR data including but not limited to the agreements between Flock, Vigilant, Axon, or any similar ALPR programs and softwares

Please segregate all non-exempt material, and “black out” rather than “white out” any exempt material. Please cite specific exemptions in every instance that  the public body claims an exemption.

Thank you so much!

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Southern Oregon Flock Off

title: Drone as First Responder and Skydio dock program records

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: Drone as First Responder and Skydio dock program records
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

In January 2026, the Federal Way City Council approved a Drone as First Responder (DFR) program using Skydio Dock for X10 systems. I request the following existing records in the Department's possession, created or modified between January 1, 2025 and the date this request is processed:

1. Contracts, purchase orders, and agreements with Skydio, including costs;
2. Records identifying the locations or siting of drone docks;
3. DFR program policies, procedures, evaluation criteria, and success metrics;
4. Privacy impact assessments or civil-liberties reviews conducted for the program;
5. Flight or deployment logs for DFR missions flown since the program began, sufficient to determine the date, time, general location, and purpose of each deployment.

This request does not seek video or imagery recorded by the drones. I prefer electronic delivery. Please notify me in advance if any copying or production fees will exceed $50.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robin Monks

communications.subject: Confirmation - P-2026-3419 (Federal Way Police Department - Police Records)
communications.communication:
Dear Robin Monks, 
  
 The Federal Way Police Department - Police Records received your request and we look forward to assisting you with your records search. 
  
 Your assigned request number and security key are listed below. Please retain this information to track the progress of your request and to download records from the Records Portal. 
  
 Request Number: Request Number: P-2026-3419  
 Security Key: ABE4ED88 
  
 When will I receive a response to my request? 
  
 City Records and Police Records Requests 
  
 The City Clerk Department is responsible for managing requests for all general city records, except those maintained by the Federal Way Police Department or the Municipal Court. The Federal Way Police Department is responsible for coordinating, tracking, and fulfilling requests for police records. Court records are addressed separately below. 
  
 Pursuant to RCW 42.56.520, you will receive a response within five (5) business days of receipt of your City or Police records request, with one of the following: 
  
 Providing the record(s); 
 Providing a link to the records posted on the City’s website; 
 Providing a reasonable estimate of the time necessary to provide records; 
 Seeking clarification of the request; or 
 Denying the request 
  
 Additional time to respond may be required to locate and assemble records, notify affected third parties, or determine whether disclosure exemptions apply. The five-day response period begins on the next business day after receipt of the request (weekends and holidays excluded). 
  
 The Public Records Act (RCW 42.56) does not require a governmental agency to create new information/records, conduct legal research, or answer questions. For more information, please view the City of Federal Way Public Records Policy.  
  
 Municipal Court Records Requests 
  
 Court records are subject to release under the WA State Court General Rules, GR 31–Access to Court Records and GR 31.1–Access to Administrative Records. Court records are not subject to the Public Records Act.   
  
 Questions? 
  
 If you have any questions, contact information for each type of record request is listed below: 
  
 Police Records
Phone: 253-835-6700
Email: PD-PRA@federalwaywa.gov

 City Records

 Thank you for using the City of Federal Way Public Records Request Center. 
  
 Sincerely, 

Police Records

RESPONSE: Documents responsive to your request are available to download via the CPS FOIA Center at www.cps.edu/FOIARequests . Please log in with your username and password to access the records. Please note that certain private information (personal descriptions, employee ID numbers, college transcripts, social security numbers, citizenship status, signatures, personal addresses/phone numbers, medical information, etc.) was redacted pursuant to 5 ILCS 140/7. Specifically, section 7(1)(b) which exempts certain private information as defined by section 2(c-5) and section 7(1)(c) which exempts personal information contained within public records, the disclosure of which would constitute a clearly unwarranted invasion of personal privacy, unless the disclosure is consented to in writing by the individual subject of the information. “Unwarranted invasion of personal privacy” means the disclosure of information that is highly personal or objectionable to a reasonable person and in which the subject’s right to privacy outweighs any legitimate public interest in obtaining the information. 5 ILCS 140/7(1)(a) exempts “ information specifically prohibited from disclosure by federal or State Law … ” (5 ILCS 140/7(1)(a)) Specifically, 105 ILCS 5/10-21.9 (b) states that “ any information concerning the record of convictions obtained by the president of the school board or the regional superintendent shall be confidential and may only be transmitted to the superintendent of the school district or his designee, the appropriate regional superintendent if the check was requested by the school district, the presidents of the appropriate school boards if the check was requested from the Department of State Police by the regional superintendent, the State Superintendent of Education, the State Teacher Certification Board, any other person necessary to the decision of hiring the applicant for employment, or for clarification purposes the Department of State Police or Statewide Sex Offender Database, or both.” 
You have a right to have the denial of your request reviewed by the Public Access Counselor (PAC) at the Office of the Illinois Attorney General. 5 ILCS 140/9.5(a). You can file your Request for Review with the PAC by writing to: Leah Bartelt; Public Access Counselor Office of the Attorney General 500 South 2nd Street Springfield, Illinois 62706 E-mail: public.access@ilag.gov 877-299-3642 You also have the right to seek judicial review of your denial by filing a lawsuit in the State circuit court. 5 ILCS 140/11. If you choose to file a Request for Review with the PAC, you must do so within 60 calendar days of the date of this denial letter. 5 ILCS 140/9.5(a). Please note that you must include a copy of your original FOIA request and this denial letter when filing a Request for Review with the PAC. Sincerely, Marisol Muneton Freedom of Information Act Officer Chicago Public Schools

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Government Records Access and Management Act, I hereby request the following records:

Related to automated license plate reader (ALPR) or "Flock Safety" camera systems operated by or in partnership with the West Valley Police and West Valley:

All contracts, agreements, memoranda of understanding, or other instruments between West Valley Police and Flock Safety, Inc., or any related entity, including any amendments or renewals. (No date restriction.)

All invoices, payment records, and purchase orders related to Flock Safety equipment, software, or services. (January 1, 2020 through present.)

All data retention policies governing footage, license plate reads, or associated metadata collected by Flock cameras. (No date restriction.)

All written policies, procedures, or general orders governing officer access to, and use of, Flock camera data. (No date restriction.)

All records reflecting the total number of Flock cameras deployed, their locations, and dates of installation. (January 1, 2020 through present.)

All records of third-party data sharing, including but not limited to agreements or logs of data shared with other law enforcement agencies, federal agencies, or private parties. (January 1, 2020 through present.)

All audit logs, access logs, or query logs reflecting searches of Flock camera data by West Valley Police employees or contractors. (January 1, 2024 through present.)

All records reflecting complaints, grievances, or legal challenges related to the Flock camera program. (January 1, 2020 through present.)

All communications, including email and internal messaging platform records, between West Valley Police employees and Flock Safety, Inc. representatives regarding the procurement, deployment, expansion, or renewal of the program. (January 1, 2024 through present.)

Any privacy impact assessments, legal reviews, or internal memoranda regarding the program's compliance with Texas law. (No date restriction.)

If any portion of a responsive record is withheld, please identify each withheld document by description, date, author, and recipient in a detailed withholding log, and specify the statutory exception claimed for each.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Emma E Metos

title: WA ALPR: A: External Access Audit Logs (1/4) (Walla Walla Police Department)

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: WA ALPR: A: External Access Audit Logs (1/4) (Walla Walla Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. All system audit logs, as natively maintained in your agency's systems or your vendor's systems, reflecting access to your agency's ALPR system or any system used to store, process, or query ALPR data (e.g., Axon Evidence.com, Flock Safety portal, Motorola/Vigilant), by users affiliated with any agency other than your agency.

2. All system audit logs, as natively maintained, reflecting the Originating Agency Identifier (ORI) or agency name associated with each external query of your agency's ALPR system.

3. All system audit logs, as natively maintained, reflecting the user identifier, badge number, or account name associated with each query of your agency's ALPR system, whether the querying user was internal or external to your agency.

4. All records identifying which external agencies are currently authorized to access, query, or receive data from your agency's ALPR system, including any configuration record, permissions list, access control list, or authorized-agency registry maintained in your ALPR platform.  If this information exists only as a display within a software interface, a screenshot, faithful reproduction, or export of that display to any available file format is an acceptable and required form of production.

Note on vendor-held records: In Rodriguez v. City of Stanwood & Sedro-Woolley (Skagit County Superior Court, Nov. 6, 2025), the court held that ALPR data held by a third-party SaaS vendor on behalf of a government agency is a public record subject to PRA disclosure. Vendor custody does not relieve your agency of its production obligation. Each request below that encompasses vendor-held records is made on this basis. Please retrieve and produce all responsive records held by your ALPR vendor(s) on your agency's behalf.

Note on record creation: I am seeking existing records only. I understand that no agency is required to create a new record in response to a PRA request. However, producing a screenshot or other faithful reproduction of an existing electronic display is not creating a new record — it is reproducing an existing one, in the same manner as photocopying or scanning a paper document. Agencies cannot evade their production obligation by characterizing screenshots of existing system displays as "new records."

I am requesting these records for research and public interest purposes, submitted through MuckRock, a nonprofit journalism platform. I request that your agency consider waiving any fees given that this request is submitted for research and public interest purposes and that electronic production of the requested records should entail minimal or no actual cost under RCW 42.56.120. For any anticipated costs, please notify me before incurring them so that I may prioritize or narrow the request. This notification requirement should not be construed as authorization to delay production of records for which no fee will be incurred pending resolution of fees for other records in this request

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Phil Mocek

communications.subject: Oklahoma Open Records Act Request: 2026 Code violations
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Oklahoma Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

copies of public records concerning municipal code-enforcement actions within the City of Norman.

Specifically, I request a digital copy, spreadsheet, or log of all residential code-enforcement violations, citations, and notices issued from January 1, 2026, through the date this request is processed.

To limit clerical search time, please provide the information in its existing electronic format, such as Excel, CSV, or a text file. I am requesting only the following fields:

- Property owner’s or responsible party’s name
- Street address
- Violation type
- Date the violation was recorded or notice was issued

If the City does not maintain a centralized spreadsheet or log containing these fields, please provide the existing underlying electronic records from which this information can be extracted.

If any responsive record does not contain the property owner’s or responsible party’s name, please provide the remaining requested fields rather than withholding the entire record.

If the estimated cost will exceed $25, please provide an itemized estimate before processing the request. I request that any fees be waived because the records will be made available to the general public and concern the enforcement of municipal health, safety, and property-maintenance laws.

If any portion of this request is denied, withheld, or redacted, please identify the specific statutory exemption under the Oklahoma Open Records Act supporting that decision and release all reasonably segregable portions of the records.

Thank you for your attention and cooperation.

Sincerely,

AJ Keys

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

AJ Keys

communications.subject: Indiana Access to Public Records Act Request: Donald Davis (Msd Decatur Township)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Indiana Access to Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Under the Indiana Access to Public Records Act § 5-14-3-1 et seq., Mirror Indy is requesting the following Records related to the following current or former employees:

Donald Davis (6155-7950)

Hiring date, termination date, compensation, commendations, assignments/job roles, disciplinary actions, factual basis for disciplinary actions and letters of resignation for the following employees. Please exclude copies of individual training certificates.

I am including the following information as a helpful reference to related case law and Public Access Counselor opinions regarding personnel records of public employees:

Indiana Supreme Court decision WTHR-TV v. Hamilton Southeastern School District states that APRA requires disclosure of the factual basis for disciplinary action, and that factual basis cannot be a bald conclusion. It also has to be sufficient for a reasonable person to understand what an employee did to deserve discipline. See the opinion starting on page 7 of the link above.

A passing reference to violation of a specific policy is not sufficient to meet this standard.

The Indiana Public Access Counselor also has addressed the topic of resignations in lieu of termination. One such opinion can be reviewed here, but simply put a resignation in lieu of a termination does not dissolve an agency’s responsibility to provide the factual basis for discipline under the public records statute.

The state’s records statute applies to all employees, regardless of wither they are probationary or not.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 7 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Emily Hopkins

Dear Ms. Hopkins,



This correspondence is intended to follow-up with you on your public
records request seeking records related to Donald Davis.  Each of your
requests will be addressed in turn:



*Your request*:  Hiring date



*Response: * The Employee Status record showing Mr. Davis' hire date is
available for a cost of $0.10.



*Your request: * Termination date



*Response: * The Employee Status record showing Mr. Davis’ separation date
is available for a cost of $0.10.



*Your request:*  Compensation



*Response*:  An Employee Status record showing Mr. Davis’ compensation and
a compensation record showing his final unused vacation days payout and
final work days payout are available for a cost of $0.10 (1 of these
records is included in those listed above)



*Your request:*  Commendations



*Response:*  No records exist in the files of the School District that are
responsive to this request.



*Your request:*  Assignments/job roles



*Response:*  The Employee Status record showing Mr. Davis’ position held
with the School District is available (included in a record listed above).



*Your request*:  Disciplinary actions and the factual basis for
disciplinary actions



*Response: * The Indiana Access to Public Records Act only requires the
release of the factual basis for a disciplinary action in which final
action has been taken and that resulted in the employee being suspended,
demoted, or discharged.  See IC 5-14-3-4(b)(8).  All other disciplinary
records are permitted to be exempted from disclosure pursuant to IC
5-14-3-4(b)(8).  No disciplinary records exist that are subject to
mandatory disclosure under Indiana law.  To the extent you are requesting
disciplinary records beyond the scope of the records that are required to
be produced, your request is denied pursuant to IC 5-14-3-4(b)(8).  The
individual authorizing this denial is the Superintendent of the
Metropolitan School District of Decatur Township, Dr. Scott Collins.



*Your request:*  Letters of resignation



*Response: * The resignation notice is available for a cost of $0.10.

The MSD of Decatur Township accepts cash/coin payments in person at 5275
Kentucky Ave. Indianapolis, IN 46221 during regular business hours of 8:00

Personal or home addresses and phone numbers have also been redacted within the provided documents pursuant to Section 14-2-6(G) (Record must relate to public business to be defined as a public record) and the Attorney General’s Inspection of Public Records Act Compliance Guide, Ninth Edition, pages 32-33 (Agency can deny a request for personal contact information because the record does not relate to public business, as it does not reveal anything about the official acts of the employees or the operations or activities of the agency). The Records below were withheld pursuant to Records relating to medical and mental health diagnoses are protected from disclosure by the Inspection of Public Records Act and the federal Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), and have therefore been withheld.  NMSA 1978, §§ 14-2-1(A) and 14-2-6; State ex rel. Newsome v. Alarid, 1977-NMSC-076, ¶ 11, 90 N.M. 790, 794; NMSA 1978, § 14-2-1(H); 45 C.F.R. §§ 164.502(a)(1) and 164.512(e)(1). Pursuant to the DC Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

TO:   Ryann Sargent, DDOT FOIA Officer <ryann.sargent@dc.gov>; Victoria Fleming, DC WATER FOIA Officer <victoria.fleming@dc.gov>CC: oig.hotline@epa.gov; richard.jackson2@dc.gov; sharon.kershbaum@dc.gov; david.gadis@dcwater.com; foia@dcwater.com; ddot.foia@dc.gov; pmendelson@dccouncil.us; callen@dccouncil.gov; serena_bellew@nps.gov; michael_donato@nps.gov; dondrae.maiden@sol.doi.gov; Square5815Oversight@gmail.com  SUBJECT: EXPEDITED FREEDOM OF INFORMATION ACT (FOIA) REQUEST: Work Orders, TOPS Permits, and Dispatch Records for Square 5815 / Morris Rd SE

Pursuant to the District of Columbia Freedom of Information Act, D.C. Official Code § 2-531 et seq., I hereby request expedited production of the following public records:

1. WORK ORDERS & ASSET MANAGEMENT: All internal DC Water work orders, service tickets, maintenance requests, and work tickets generated within DC Water’s enterprise asset management system (e.g., Maximo) from September 1, 2026, through October 4, 2026, concerning Square 5815, Lot 802, 16th St SE, or the adjacent public right-of-way.

   - Reason: "Sewer Emergency Repair"

   - Contact Telephone Number: (202) 612-3400

communications.communication:
Here's the documentation. This was given to another department in another state, so pardon any differences in context:

Steps for exporting email metadata from Office 365:
0. Username must have access to search and export eDiscovery reports. If not, your IT department should have access to either grant the required permissions, or run through these steps themselves.
1. From Internet Explorer, log into https://protection.office.com/. 
2. Navigate to "Search & Investigation" -> "eDiscovery" and create a new case.
3. Open the case, then create a new search through "Search" -> "New search"
4. Add a "Type" condition and select, "E-mail messages".
5. Under "Locations" -> "Specific locations" -> "Modify...".
6. Toggle the location that includes "Exchange email" and click "Save".
7. Click "Save & run" and give the search a name.
8. Navigate to "More" -> "Export results", then select the following options:
-Output options: "All items, excluding [...]"
-Export Exchange content as: "Individual messages"
9. Navigate to Export -> "[Name of export]_Export".
10. Click "Download results" and launch the "Unified Export Tool".
11. Paste the export page's "Export key" into the tool's key field.
12. Choose a save location and click "Start"
13. Open "results.csv" from the saved location.
14. Delete all columns that are not the requested metadata and save.

(Please note that depending on the size of the csv files, this may need to be done in batches through the use of a date or sender/receiver conditional within the search query. Similar can be said about filtering down to just your office's department's email addresses.)

 Your request under the Freedom of Information Law (FOIL) is denied in part and granted in part for the reasons stated below. 
  * Granted in part because responsive records - i.e., RESULTS1 to RESULTS35 - are being disclosed to you on the OpenRecords portal and otherwise denied because the records you requested are exempt from disclosure under FOIL because if disclosed, the records would constitute: (i) an unwarranted invasion of privacy and/or (ii) inter- or intra-agency materials which are not facts, staff instructions affecting the public, final policy, final determination, or external audits. communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: C-Star Contracts and Devices
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Regarding the C-STAR project (https://www.king5.com/article/news/local/seattle-convention-center-seattle-police-launch-new-downtown-public-safety-hub/281-0ebe16ce-23bb-4f71-a499-733f332d69dd), please provide the following:
1. Contracts, MOUs, MOAs, NDAs, invoices, and other agreements with any of the following: Seattle Police Department, Flock, Axon, Motorola, Genetec, Verkada, Briefcam, Auror.
2. A list of cameras, automatic license plate readers, and gunshot detection systems installed as part of C-STAR or whose data is connected/accessible from C-STAR sufficient to discern the locations and device type of each device.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Rose Terse

communications.subject: RE: Washington Public Records Act Request: C-Star Contracts and Devices
communications.communication:
Hello Hannah,

Respectfully, RCW 42.56.080(2) does not require requesters to complete forms provided by the agency in order to process the request: "Agencies shall honor requests received in person during an agency's normal office hours, or by mail or email, for identifiable public records unless exempted by provisions of this chapter. No official format is required for making a records request; however, agencies may recommend that requestors submit requests using an agency provided form or web page."

I am declining to complete your agency recommended form and ask that you fulfill my request as submitted and provide responsive records via email.

Thank you,
Rose
